_comment: DUO-3222/DUO-3227: the ONE project-level WordPress/PHP/database compatibility statement. PHP and database use min-inclusive/max-exclusive ranges; WordPress uses the same min-inclusive/max-exclusive range narrowed to the exercised series named in verified, so a core inside the range whose MAJOR.MINOR was never exercised is still refused rather than claimed. The agent pre-policy gate and duo doctor block outside these values, and tools/capability-doc.php cross-checks this file against manifests/capabilities/platform.json so the two copies cannot drift -- never independently-maintained numbers.

php.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's own Docker tags (wordpress:7.0.3-php8.3-apache / wordpress:cli-php8.3 -- see sandbox/pair.yml, sandbox/db.yml, sandbox/docker-compose.yml). Verified live: PHP 8.3.33 as of this writing.

database.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's own Docker tag (mariadb:11 -- see sandbox/db.yml, sandbox/docker-compose.yml). Verified live: 11.8.8-MariaDB as of this writing. MySQL is not claimed or tested against; a site running MySQL instead of MariaDB is genuinely untested, not merely unpinned.

wordpress.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's exact Docker tags: each key of verified is a core series, and its value is the exact patch a full live proof ran on (6.9 on wordpress:6.9.2-php8.3-apache, 7.0 on wordpress:7.0.3-php8.3-apache -- sandbox/tests/live/regress_core_scope_platform.sh, regress_core_data_boundary.sh, conformance-core). A core is accepted only when it is inside [6.9.0, 7.1.0) AND its MAJOR.MINOR is one of those exercised series, so an unexercised minor line inside the range is still refused rather than claimed by a bare range. Patches inside an exercised series are claimed on exactly the basis PHP 8.3.x and MariaDB 11.x already are here -- one measured runtime per line. last_verified is the newest exercised core and the one sandbox/pair.yml boots by default.
